mainTopic: Broken and dislocated limbs in birds and animals, whether a bird's lung can make it טריפה, and רב's rulings on a dislocated thigh
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a man whose insides came out and who still survived. Then it returns to the משנה's case of a bird with broken legs: רבא checks such birds at the צומת הגידין and rules them כשר. רב lists which dislocated limbs make an animal or bird טריפה. For a dislocated wing, he worries the lung was punctured, while שמואל and רבי יוחנן say to check it. חזקיה says a bird has no lung, and רבי יוחנן says it does. The גמרא tries several softer readings of חזקיה, but in the end concludes he simply was not familiar with chickens. Next come two opposite reports of רב on a bird with a dislocated thigh. רב הונא explains that each place follows its own custom. A story with רבי אבא and רב ירמיה בר אבא then shows that רב distinguished a thigh that slipped out (כשרה) from one that was cut (פסולה). Finally, in ארץ ישראל, רבי אבא hears רבי זירא quote רב as saying טריפה, and his reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: the father faints and is sewn up
steps.stepSummary: The story from the previous lines ends. The Roman only pretended to kill the son, the father fainted, his intestines slipped back in, and his stomach was sewn shut.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was only a trick of the eyes. The father fainted and went limp, his intestines went back inside, and the Roman sewed up his stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story it started before this section. The story shows that someone can survive even when their insides come out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fake killing scared the father so badly that he fainted. When his body went limp, his intestines slid back into place, which let the Roman sew him up. The story backs up the earlier idea that this kind of injury is not always fatal.

keyTerms.meaning: A trick of the eyes; something done only for show

phrases.english: Deceptively (only pretending to kill the son),
the father fainted and went limp,
his intestines went back in
phrases.notes: Some versions spell it like the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling. Both mean 'his intestines.'

phrases.english: and he sewed up his stomach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father survived. His intestines went back in and his stomach was sewn up.

steps.title: רבא checks a basket of birds with broken legs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a bird whose legs broke. רבא checked such birds at the place where the sinews meet and ruled them כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'if its legs broke.' A basket of birds came before רבא. He checked them at the meeting point of the sinews and declared them כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a bird with broken legs. It tells how רבא ruled in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Broken legs alone do not make a bird טריפה. What matters is the area where the sinews come together. Since רבא found that area undamaged, the birds were כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its legs were broken (a quote from the משנה)
The place where the sinews in the leg come together

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'If its legs were broken.'
There was a certain basket of birds
that came before Rava.
Rava checked it at the convergence of the sinews,
and declared it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird with broken legs is כשר if the meeting point of the sinews is undamaged.

steps.title: רב's rulings on dislocated limbs
steps.stepSummary: רב says a dislocated foreleg in an animal is כשר. A dislocated thigh in an animal or a bird, or a dislocated wing in a bird, makes it טריפה, because we worry the lung was punctured.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A dislocated foreleg in an animal is כשר. A dislocated thigh in an animal is טריפה. A dislocated thigh in a bird is טריפה. A dislocated wing in a bird is טריפה, because we worry the lung was punctured.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a list of rulings about limbs that have popped out of place. Some are כשר and some are טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's foreleg is fine, but a thigh is a problem in both animals and birds. For a bird's wing, the reason is a worry: the wing is close to the lung, so pulling it out may have damaged the lung. רב does not ask us to check; he simply assumes the worst.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
We are concerned; we worry that

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A dislocated foreleg in an animal: kosher.
A dislocated thigh in an animal: tereifa.
A dislocated thigh in a bird: tereifa.
A dislocated wing in a bird: tereifa,
because we worry that perhaps the lung was punctured.
phrases.notes: This reason is for the wing. The lung sits right near where the wing attaches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָד בַּבְּהֵמָה – כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from broken legs to limbs that are pulled out of place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dislocated foreleg in an animal is כשר. A dislocated thigh in an animal or bird, or a dislocated wing in a bird, is טריפה, out of concern for the lung.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן: check the lung
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב about the wing. He says we should check the lung, and רבי יוחנן agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: it should be checked. רבי יוחנן also says: it should be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion argues with רב about the dislocated wing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב assumes the lung may be punctured and declares the bird טריפה without looking. שמואל and רבי יוחנן say to check the lung instead; if it is fine, the bird is כשר. The disagreement is whether we just worry or actually check.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; agreeing with the previous view

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument shapes how a bird with a dislocated wing is treated: is it automatically forbidden, or can it be saved by checking the lung?

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It should be checked,
and so said Rabbi Yochanan: It should be checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's last ruling about the dislocated wing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a dislocated wing, check the lung. If it is not punctured, the bird is כשר.

steps.title: Does a bird have a lung?
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says a bird has no lung. רבי יוחנן says it does, and that it looks like a rose petal between the wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה says: a bird has no lung. רבי יוחנן says: it does have one, and it looks like a rose petal, between the wings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new argument begins about whether birds even have a lung. This matters for everything just said about checking a bird's lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gives a physical description: the lung is thin and red like a rose petal, located between the wings. חזקיה's statement sounds strange, so the גמרא will next ask what he really means.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said: A bird has no lung.
And Rabbi Yochanan said: It does have one,
and it is like a rose petal,
between the wings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected to the lung worry in steps 3 and 4, but opens a separate argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: a bird has no lung. רבי יוחנן: it has a lung, like a rose petal, between the wings.

steps.title: What did חזקיה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חזקיה meant by saying a bird has no lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'a bird has no lung' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about חזקיה's words. It is setting up the next moves, where it will try out possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, חזקיה's words are hard to accept. So the גמרא looks for the real meaning of his statement.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'a bird has no lung'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of חזקיה's statement in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly חזקיה meant when he said a bird has no lung.

steps.title: It can't mean birds have no lung at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the literal meaning, that birds have no lung at all, and rejects it because we can see that they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it has none at all, we can see that it does have one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simplest reading of חזקיה and throws it out right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can open a bird and see a lung. So חזקיה could not have meant that birds have no lung at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say; suggesting a possible meaning
We see with our own eyes

phrases.english: If you say that it has none at all,
but we see that it does have one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one answer to the question in step 6 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the literal reading of חזקיה's words.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against what we can plainly see: birds do have lungs.

steps.title: Maybe he means a lung problem doesn't make a bird טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new reading: חזקיה meant that a damaged lung does not make a bird טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means that the bird does not become טריפה through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible meaning for חזקיה. It is setting up the next step, where this reading will be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, 'no lung' means the lung does not count for טריפה purposes in a bird. Even if it is punctured, the bird would stay כשר.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that the bird does not become a tereifa through it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected literal reading with a halachic one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיה meant that a damaged lung does not make a bird טריפה.

steps.title: Levi's ברייתא: bird טריפות match animal טריפות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading with a ברייתא of לוי. Every טריפה in an animal also applies to a bird, and birds have one extra: a broken skull bone. So a punctured lung should make a bird טריפה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But לוי taught: the טריפות the חכמים listed for animals apply the same way to birds. Birds have one more: if the skull bone broke, even though the brain's covering was not punctured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 8 using a teaching of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A punctured lung is a טריפה in animals. לוי says all animal טריפות count for birds as well, so a punctured lung should make a bird טריפה. That contradicts the idea that חזקיה meant a bird's lung never makes it טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to them; the same ones

steps.confusionAlert: The skull case is an extra טריפה only for birds. In an animal, the brain's covering must be punctured; in a bird, a broken skull bone is enough. The point here is the first half of the ברייתא: every animal טריפה applies to birds.

phrases.english: But didn't Levi teach:
The tereifot that the Sages listed in an animal,
the same ones apply in a bird,
and in addition to them, a bird is a tereifa if
the bone of the skull was broken,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ!
phrases.english: even though the membrane of the brain was not punctured!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי לֵוִי: טְרֵפוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים בַּבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of חזקיה offered in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that חזקיה meant a punctured lung does not make a bird טריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי teaches that every animal טריפה also applies to birds. A punctured lung is an animal טריפה, so it must also make a bird טריפה.

steps.title: A new reading: the lung does not need checking after a fall or burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from לוי's ברייתא by reading חזקיה differently: he meant that a bird's lung has no rules of falling or singeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, חזקיה meant that a bird's lung has no rule of 'falling' and no rule of 'singeing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The previous reading failed, so the גמרא offers a narrower reading of חזקיה's words. He did not mean that a damaged lung never makes a bird טריפה. He only meant that the lung does not need checking after a fall or a burn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's ברייתא proved that a punctured lung does make a bird טריפה. So the גמרא shrinks חזקיה's claim: a real hole still makes it טריפה. But we do not have to worry that the lung was damaged just because the bird fell or was in a fire.

keyTerms.meaning: To fall; the rule that an animal that fell must be checked for inner damage
To be singed; the rule that an animal caught in a fire must be checked for burned organs
It has no (rule of); here it means the rule does not apply to it

phrases.english: Rather, it has no rule of falling
phrases.notes: He means the bird's lung does not need to be checked after the bird falls.

phrases.english: and no rule of singeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֵין לוֹ לֹא לִינָּפֵל וְלֹא לֵיחָמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing what חזקיה meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה meant that a damaged lung never makes a bird טריפה
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה only meant that the lung does not need checking after a fall or burning

steps.title: Why the lung needs no checking: the ribs protect it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this rule, and רב חנה explains that most of the bird's ribs shield the lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? רב חנה said: because most of its ribs protect it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a bird's lung is not checked after a fall or a burn. רב חנה answers that the lung is well protected by the ribs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling or burning is a worry only if the organ could really be hurt. In a bird, most of the ribs cover the lung, so a fall or fire is not likely to reach it. That is why there is nothing to check.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Rav Ḥana said:
Since the majority of its ribs
protect it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the reading offered in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a bird's lung needs no checking after falling or burning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most of the bird's ribs protect the lung

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reply shows חזקיה meant there is no lung at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: רבי יוחנן answered that a bird does have a lung, so חזקיה must have said it has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since רבי יוחנן said 'it does have one, and it is like a rose petal between the wings,' we learn that חזקיה held it has no lung at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading by looking at רבי יוחנן's answer to חזקיה. His answer only makes sense if חזקיה said birds have no lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חזקיה only meant that the lung needs no checking, רבי יוחנן would not reply by describing what the lung looks like. His reply, 'it does have one,' proves the argument was about whether a lung exists at all. So every softer reading of חזקיה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; from this we can learn

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יֵשׁ לוֹ,
phrases.english: But from the fact that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It does have one,
and it is like a rose petal
between the wings –
we can infer that Ḥizkiyya holds that it does not have one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reinterpretation of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that חזקיה meant the lung needs no checking after falling or singeing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's reply ('it does have one') only fits if חזקיה denied the lung exists at all

steps.title: חזקיה simply was not familiar with chickens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives up on reinterpreting חזקיה and quotes the scholars of ארץ ישראל: his words show he was not expert in chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they say in the West in the name of רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא: from the words of the Distinguished One it is clear that he was not familiar with chickens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the search for a different meaning. It accepts that חזקיה really meant birds have no lung, and explains that he was simply wrong about the facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every attempt to rescue חזקיה failed, so the גמרא goes back to the literal reading it rejected in step 7. That reading was rejected because birds clearly have a lung. Now the גמרא accepts it anyway and explains the mistake: חזקיה lacked hands-on knowledge of birds.

keyTerms.meaning: The West; the scholars of ארץ ישראל
The Distinguished One; a title of honor for חזקיה

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, חזקיה is read literally: he said birds have no lung, and the גמרא says he was simply not familiar with chickens. רבי יוחנן is right that a bird has a lung.

phrases.english: Rather, they say in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina:
From the words of the Distinguished One it is apparent
that he is not familiar with chickens.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 12 and closes the discussion of חזקיה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חזקיה meant literally that birds have no lung, and he was mistaken because he was not familiar with chickens

steps.title: A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רב הונא quotes רב that a bird whose thigh bone slipped out of its socket is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about birds. רב rules that a bird whose thigh bone came out of its socket is still כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh ruling about a specific bird injury. It is stated simply, and the next steps will test it against a different report of רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A dislocated thigh; the thigh bone slipped out of its socket

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the dislocated thigh in a bird from step 3, now with רב הונא's opposite report of רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird with a dislocated thigh is כשרה

steps.title: A conflicting report from פומבדיתא says it is טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא challenges his father with a report from the scholars of פומבדיתא: רב said a dislocated thigh in a bird is טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said to רב הונא: But the scholars who came from פומבדיתא said that רב יהודה said in the name of רב: a dislocated thigh in a bird is טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's own son raises a contradiction. Another student of רב reported the exact opposite ruling in רב's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports quote the same teacher, רב, on the same case, but with opposite results: כשרה versus טריפה. So it seems one of the reports must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal injury; forbidden to eat
פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in Babylonia

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said to Rav Huna:
But the Rabbis who came from Pumbedita said
that Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is a tereifa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 14 with a conflicting report
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that רב ruled a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה reports the opposite ruling from the same teacher, רב

steps.title: Each place follows its own custom
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that each river has its own course: רב ruled according to the custom of each place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My son, each river has its own course.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא settles the contradiction by saying both reports are true. Each place follows its own custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports are accurate. רב himself held that the bird is כשרה. But for the people of פומבדיתא, who were strict, he ruled טריפה to match their custom.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one report is a mistake. Both are what רב said; they were rulings for different communities.

phrases.english: He said to him: My son,
each river and its course.
phrases.notes: A saying: every place keeps its own custom, just as every river flows its own way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reports true; different rulings for different local customs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רב's ruling contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: רב held כשרה, but ruled טריפה for פומבדיתא according to their custom

steps.title: Why check the צומת הגידין if a dislocated thigh is kosher?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא finds רב ירמיה בר אבא checking birds at the צומת הגידין and challenges him from רב's ruling that a dislocated thigh is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא went and found רב ירמיה בר אבא checking birds at the צומת הגידין. He said to him: Why does the master need all this? Didn't רב הונא say in the name of רב that a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a challenge. רבי אבא sees that רב ירמיה checks a spot in the bird's thigh and asks why, given רב's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא is reasoning from the bigger case to the smaller one. If a bird is כשרה even when its whole thigh bone is out of place, a problem at the צומת הגידין should not matter either. So the checking seems like extra work.

keyTerms.meaning: The place in the thigh where the sinews come together
Master; a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַבִּי אַבָּא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba went and found Rav Yirmeya bar Abba
inspecting at the convergence of sinews.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמָר כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why does the master need all this?
But didn't Rav Huna say that Rav said:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמָר כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָא רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of step 14 to question a practice
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ירמיה בר אבא's practice of checking the צומת הגידין in birds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a whole dislocated thigh is כשרה, a problem at the צומת הגידין should surely not make the bird טריפה

steps.title: The משנה and רב say the צומת הגידין rule applies to birds too
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה answers from the משנה: an animal whose צומת הגידין was removed is טריפה, and רב said the same applies to a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I know the משנה: an animal whose legs were cut off from the knee joint and below is kosher; from the knee joint and above, it is unfit. And the same if the צומת הגידין was removed. And רב said about this: and the same for a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה defends his practice with a משנה and a ruling of רב. Removing the צומת הגידין makes an animal טריפה, and רב said this is true for birds as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever the rule is for a dislocated thigh, רב himself clearly said a removed צומת הגידין makes a bird טריפה. So checking that spot is needed. A lenient ruling about one injury does not cancel a separate, explicit ruling about another.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same applies to a bird

steps.whatToRemember: Even though רב held that a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה, a bird whose צומת הגידין was removed is טריפה. So that spot must still be checked.

phrases.english: He said to him: I know the mishna:
An animal whose legs were cut off,
from the leg joint and below, is kosher;
from the leg joint and above, it is unfit;
and likewise if the convergence of sinews was removed,
and Rav said about it: And likewise with a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge from step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing an explicit משנה and a ruling of רב that covers this case directly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a dislocated thigh is כשרה, the צומת הגידין need not be checked
steps.terutzMaskana: A removed צומת הגידין makes a bird טריפה, as רב said, so checking it is needed

steps.title: רב's two rulings seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects: if רב said that removing the צומת הגידין makes a bird טריפה, that clashes with רב's ruling that a bird with a dislocated thigh is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a contradiction between one statement of רב and another statement of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא hears רב ירמיה's answer and points out that it creates a new problem. Now רב seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה just said that, according to רב, a bird whose צומת הגידין was removed is טריפה. But רב also said that a bird whose thigh slipped out of its socket is כשרה. Both injuries are in the thigh area, so it seems strange that one is טריפה and the other is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
One statement of רב contradicts another statement of רב
The place where the sinews of the thigh come together
A thigh bone that slipped out of its socket

phrases.english: If so,
there is a contradiction between Rav and Rav!
phrases.notes: One of רב's rulings says the צומת הגידין makes a bird טריפה; the other says a dislocated thigh is כשרה (Step 14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב ירמיה's answer into a new challenge, because it creates an internal contradiction in רב's rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's two rulings: a dislocated thigh is כשרה, and a removed צומת הגידין is טריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are injuries at the thigh, so ruling one כשרה and the other טריפה seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Silence, then a suggested distinction between slipped out and cut
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה is silent. רבי אבא himself suggests that רב may distinguish between a thigh that slipped out and one that was cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. He said to him: Perhaps רב makes a difference between a thigh that slipped out and one that was cut?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה has no answer, so רבי אבא offers a possible way to fix the contradiction himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer is that the two cases are not the same kind of injury. When the thigh only slipped out of its socket, nothing was cut, so the bird can be כשרה. When it is cut, the bird is טריפה. The suggestion is only phrased as a possibility (דלמא), which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference for him; he distinguishes

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רב ירמיה, who had no answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps there is a difference for him
phrases.notes: Now רבי אבא is speaking, and 'him' means רב.

phrases.english: between one that slipped out and one that was cut?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ בֵּין שְׁמוּטָה לַחֲתוּכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the contradiction raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (slipped out vs. cut)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every injury to the thigh should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: A thigh that only slipped out is different from one that was cut.

steps.title: רב said the distinction explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה answers that there is no need to guess. רב himself said explicitly: slipped out is כשרה, cut is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you explaining רב's teachings on your own? רב said it explicitly: one that slipped out is כשרה; one that was cut is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה confirms רבי אבא's suggestion. He says it is not just a guess, because רב said it in clear words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distinction moves from a suggestion to a stated ruling of רב. This settles the contradiction: the כשרה ruling is about a thigh that slipped out, and the טריפה ruling is about one that was cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit, not allowed to be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a bird's thigh that slipped out of its socket is כשרה, but one that was cut is פסולה.

phrases.english: He said to him: And are you explaining
the teachings of Rav?
Rav said explicitly:
One that slipped out is kosher,
one that was cut is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ מְפָרְשַׁתְּ שְׁמַעְתָּתֵיהּ דְּרַב? בְּפֵירוּשׁ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the suggested distinction from Step 20 with an explicit statement of רב.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between a thigh that slipped out and one that was cut.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An explicit ruling of רב: שמוטה כשרה, חתוכה פסולה.

steps.title: Do not be surprised: where and how you cut matters
steps.stepSummary: The explicit statement of רב continues: it is not strange for two similar-looking injuries to have opposite results. Cutting in one place kills an animal, while cutting in another place does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not be surprised, because you can cut it in one place and it dies, and cut it in another place and it lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The quote from רב continues with his reason. It answers a question the learner might still have: how can two injuries so close together have opposite results?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might still feel that a slipped thigh and a cut thigh are too alike to be treated differently. The answer is that small differences in the kind or place of an injury really do decide whether a living creature survives. That makes the different rulings reasonable.

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for one cuts it from here and it dies,
one cuts it from here and it lives.
phrases.notes: The same word מִכָּאן ('from here') is repeated, but it means a different spot this time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי חוֹתְכָהּ מִכָּאן וָמֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's explicit statement quoted in Step 21 and gives the reason behind its distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answers an unspoken question with a reason from real life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two injuries so close to each other should have the same result.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exact place and type of an injury can decide between death and life.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא quotes רב that a dislocated thigh is טריפה
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אבא goes up to ארץ ישראל, he finds רבי זירא teaching in the name of רב הונא, who quoted רב, that a bird with a dislocated thigh is טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבא went up, he found רבי זירא sitting and saying: רב הונא said in the name of רב: a bird with a dislocated thigh is טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי אבא hears a version of רב's ruling that is the opposite of what we learned before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in Step 14, רב הונא quoted רב that a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה. Now רבי זירא quotes the same chain, רב הונא in the name of רב, saying it is טריפה. This sets up רבי אבא's reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
An animal or bird with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reports. In Step 14, רב הונא quoted רב as saying כשרה. Here רבי זירא quotes רב הונא in the name of רב as saying טריפה.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Abba went up,
phrases.notes: 'Went up' means he moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Zeira
sitting and saying:
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי אַבָּא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that brings an opposite report of רב's ruling from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי זירא's report of רב הונא in the name of רב, a bird with a dislocated thigh is טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This report clashes with the earlier one that a dislocated thigh is כשרה, so the גמרא will need to sort out what רב really said.

steps.title: רבי אבא begins to respond to רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא starts his reaction with an oath: 'By the Master's life, since the day the Master came up here…'. His sentence continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your life, Master, since the day you came up here…
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up רבי אבא's challenge to רבי זירא's report. The sentence is not finished yet and continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong opening, swearing by רבי זירא's life, shows that רבי אבא is surprised by what he heard. He points to the day רבי זירא came up to ארץ ישראל. What he means by this is spelled out when his sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: By the life of the Master (a polite oath)

phrases.english: He said to him: By the Master's life,
phrases.notes: רבי אבא is speaking to רבי זירא and calls him 'Master' out of respect.

phrases.english: since the day that the Master came up to here
phrases.notes: 'Here' is ארץ ישראל. The sentence keeps going in the next part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיֵּי דְּמָר, מִיּוֹמָא דִּסְלֵיק מָר לְהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי אבא's reaction to רבי זירא's report in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's report that רב said a dislocated thigh in a bird is טריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The challenge is just starting. רבי אבא points to the time since רבי זירא came to ארץ ישראל, and the full point continues next.
